goal: Find QCMI=0 with non-Clifford Cartan parameters under non-aligned axes

wall_claim.statement: For non-aligned Cartan axes, QCMI=0 if and only if all c_j in (pi/2)Z
wall_claim.reverse: QCMI=0 => c_j in (pi/2)Z (UNKNOWN, this is the wall)
wall_claim.aligned_case: For aligned axes: reverse holds strictly (proven)

executive_summary.counterexample: All-X axis configuration at p=0.5: any c with all 4 axes = +/-x_hat gives QCMI=0
executive_summary.qualification: Counterexample requires p=0.5 (maximally mixed environment). For p != 0.5, all-X QCMI > 0.

counterexample.description: b1=1 vertex-sharing chain, all 4 Cartan axes = +/-x_hat, p=0.5, any c

configuration.c: Any c in (0, pi) - verified for 30 values from 0.1 to 3.0
configuration.axes: All 4 edges: +/-x_hat = [+/-1, 0, 0]. Any combination of +x and -x works.

verification.gram_matrix: Single non-zero eigenvalue -> all Kraus operators proportional
verification.b1_2_extension: Also works for b1=2 (8 edges all X, QCMI=8.41e-11)
verification.z2_gauge: Stable under any combination of +/-X signs
verification.fragility: Adding 1e-4 Z component -> QCMI rises to 1.33e-7
verification.p_dependence: QCMI=0 ONLY at p=0.5. At p=0.3: QCMI=0.39. At p=0.1: QCMI=1.05.

mechanism.level_1: At p=0.5, environment state is |+> = (|0>+|1>)/sqrt(2), the +1 eigenstate of X.
mechanism.level_2: Cartan gate U(c,x) = cos(c)*I + i*sin(c)*X*X. On |+>: X|+> = |+>.
mechanism.level_3: Effectively: U acts as cos(c)*I + i*sin(c)*X_sys on the system, leaving env unchanged.
mechanism.level_4: Since env never changes state, all Kraus operators are proportional -> QCMI = 0.
mechanism.deep: The wall holds for generic p != 0.5. At p=0.5, the X-basis provides a decoupled representation.

task1_systematic_scan.method: Grid c (60 points) x random axes (3000 each) = 180K configs
task1_systematic_scan.result: NO counterexample found by random sampling
task1_systematic_scan.random_floor_c05: 0.34 bits (min among 100K random samples at c=0.5)
task1_systematic_scan.random_floor_any_c: 0.0176 bits (at c=0.05, near c=0 Clifford point)

task2_symmetry_search.method: 6 symmetry classes, 25 c points x 1500 configs each
task2_symmetry_search.result: All classes find minimum at Clifford point. Symmetry alone insufficient.
task2_symmetry_search.key_finding: Global rotation invariance violated: env initial state fixed in Z basis.

2a_coplanar.description: All axes in xz-plane (phi=0), random theta

2b_orthogonal_groups.description: E1 edges share n1, E2 edges share n2, n1·n2=0

2c_exchange_symmetry.description: Edges 0 and 3 share n_even, edges 1 and 2 share n_odd (exchange symmetric)

2e_per_qubit_consistent.description: All edges share same axis (global rotation) -> QCMI invariant
2e_per_qubit_consistent.verdict: QCMI invariant under global rotation, as expected from symmetry

2f_angle_60.description: E1 edges share n1, E2 edges share n2, angle(n1,n2)=60°

task2g_deep_dive.method: Local perturbation around 30 best candidates, 3000 perturbations each
task2g_deep_dive.result: Perturbation optimizer DISCOVERED all-X counterexample by rotating axes toward +/-x_hat.

task2h_gradient_descent.method: Gradient descent in 9-dim space, 30 starts x 150 steps
task2h_gradient_descent.reason: Converged to c=1.570684 (0.0001 from pi/2). Clifford noise, not counterexample.

task3_b2_scan.method: b1=2 system (7 qubits, 8 edges), 15 c points x 300 random axes = 4.5K configs
task3_b2_scan.result: Random: minimum at Clifford. All-X: QCMI=0 at p=0.5 for all c.

task4_cross_p.method: Random axis scan for 5 c values at 3 p levels
task4_cross_p.key_finding: QCMI landscape scales with p but character unchanged.

gradient_descent.analysis: c is within 0.0001 of pi/2 (Clifford). Numerical noise, not a counterexample.
gradient_descent.lesson: Gradient descent converged to trivial Clifford zero. Must check c value.

synthesis.counterexample_family: Any c with all-X axes at p=0.5 -> QCMI=0
synthesis.strong_form: QCMI=0 => c_j in (pi/2)Z for ALL axis configs at generic p
synthesis.strong_form_status: LIKELY TRUE for p != 0.5, but no proof
synthesis.weak_form: For generic (p, axes), QCMI=0 only at Clifford c
synthesis.weak_form_status: SUPPORTED by ~500K configs: no non-Clifford non-X counterexample found
open_questions: Does any non-X axis config give QCMI=0 for non-Clifford c at p=0.5?
For p != 0.5, can QCMI be made arbitrarily small with optimized axes?
